title: Drosophila Egg Dechorionation
author: Katy M Monteith
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vcze2x6

steps.title: Build egg dechorionator
steps.instruction: In a fume hood heat a soldering iron for a few minutes, then melt the plastic around the circumference of a 50 mL Falcon tube no more than 2 inches from the bottom and discard the bottom; melt the plastic around the lid top until the centre pops out and discard the centre; after cooling, place a small square of gauze around the tube top and screw the lid back on, creating the dechorionator.

steps.title: Prepare apple agar plates
steps.instruction: Prepare apple‑agar embryo collection petri dishes according to the recipe by Katy M. Monteith.

steps.title: Set up egg cage
steps.instruction: Set up the egg cage with the appropriate flies as described in the Drosophila embryo collection protocol, perform steps 1‑4 of that protocol, and finish by removing any debris or dead flies from the petri dish using soft tweezers.

steps.title: Submerge agar and dislodge eggs
steps.instruction: Pour triple‑distilled water into the petri dish until the agar is fully submerged, then gently use a paintbrush to dislodge the eggs from the agar surface.

steps.title: Collect eggs on gauze
steps.instruction: Place the egg dechorionator in an empty beaker, pour the water/egg suspension from the petri dish into it, allowing the eggs to collect on the gauze while the water flows through into the beaker.

steps.title: Repeat collection if needed
steps.instruction: If any eggs remain on the agar surface, repeat the submerge‑dislodge (step 4) and collect (step 5) actions until no eggs remain.

steps.title: Set up bleach and water stations
steps.instruction: In a laminar flow hood place two 250 mL beakers: one containing ~90 mL of 7‑10 % bleach and the other ~90 mL of triple‑distilled water; also have hard tweezers, a paintbrush, a timer, and premade autoclaved food tubes ready.

steps.title: Transfer dechorionator to bleach
steps.instruction: Using hard tweezers, pick up the egg dechorionator and immediately place it into the bleach beaker within the flow hood.

steps.title: Bleach agitation first wash
steps.instruction: Gently and periodically move the dechorionator up and down in the bleach for 2 min 30 sec, ensuring the eggs remain fully submerged.

steps.title: Second bleach wash
steps.instruction: Discard the used bleach, add another ~90 mL of fresh 7‑10 % bleach to the beaker, and repeat the 2 min 30 sec up‑and‑down agitation.

steps.title: Rinse in distilled water
steps.instruction: Move the dechorionator directly from bleach into the triple‑distilled water beaker, agitate gently for ~30 seconds, discard the water, and repeat this rinse two additional times (total three rinses) until all bleach is removed.

steps.title: Transfer dechorionated eggs
steps.instruction: Within the laminar flow hood, either (a) use a paintbrush to move the eggs from the dechorionator directly into autoclaved food vials/bottles, or (b) resuspend the eggs in triple‑distilled water in a Falcon tube and dispense into food vials/bottles following steps 6‑8 of the Drosophila embryo collection protocol, depending on whether density control is required.

steps.title: Verify dechorionation (optional)
steps.instruction: Inspect the eggs under a microscope; successfully dechorionated eggs appear as smooth, elongated ovoids lacking dorsal appendages.
